answer: An agent economy can require every identity to place a refundable bond in a shared escrow before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. When a verified counterparty proves that an agent double-spent a task, the protocol slashes its bond and pays part to the challenger. Creating a hundred aliases then means locking a hundred bonds, not merely generating names; the attacker risks real capital for each identity and must keep it tied up throughout the voyage, whether its agents operate near a lagoon or trade walnut data.
